et soundtrack.explanation: "Et soundtrack" means "a soundtrack". To say you listen to the music from a film, use "at lytte til" (to listen to): "Jeg lytter til soundtracket" (I am listening to the soundtrack).

et soveværelse.explanation: "Et soveværelse" means "a bedroom". It is built from "at sove" (to sleep) and "et værelse" (a room). "Sove" also appears in "en sovepose" (a sleeping bag).

et speciale.explanation: "Et speciale" means "a specialty / master's thesis". When you talk about what a restaurant or a person is best at, it means "specialty": "husets speciale" (the house specialty). When you talk about the large final project of a university degree, it means "master's thesis": "Jeg afleverer mit speciale i juni" (I am handing in my thesis in June).

et spejl.explanation: "Et spejl" means "a mirror". To say you see yourself in the mirror, use "se sig selv i spejlet" (to see yourself in the mirror): "Hun ser sig selv i spejlet" (She sees herself in the mirror).

et spejlæg.explanation: "Et spejlæg" means "a fried egg". It is built from "et spejl" (a mirror) and "et æg" (an egg).

et spil.explanation: "Et spil" means "a game". It comes from "at spille" (to play). To say you play a game, use "at spille": "at spille skak" (to play chess). To say you play an instrument, use the same verb: "at spille guitar" (to play guitar).

et spindelvæv.explanation: "Et spindelvæv" means "a spiderweb". It is built from "spindel" (spider) and "et væv" (a woven fabric).

et spisebord.explanation: "Et spisebord" means "a dining table". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "et bord" (a table). "Spise" also appears in "en spiseske" (a tablespoon).

et spisekammer.explanation: "Et spisekammer" means "a pantry". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "et kammer" (a chamber).

et spisested.explanation: "Et spisested" means "an eatery". It is built from "at spise" (to eat) and "et sted" (a place). To ask for somewhere to eat nearby, say: "Er der et spisested i nærheden?" (Is there an eatery nearby?)

et spor.explanation: "Et spor" means "a track / a trace". When you talk about marks left behind, it means "a trace" or "a track": "Der er spor i sneen" (There are tracks in the snow). When you say where a train leaves from, it means "track": "Toget afgår fra spor 3" (The train leaves from track 3).

et springvand.explanation: "Et springvand" means "a fountain". It is built from "at springe" (to jump) and "vand" (water).

et sprog.explanation: "Et sprog" means "a language". To say how many languages someone speaks, use "at tale" (to speak): "Hun taler tre sprog" (She speaks three languages).

et sprogcenter.explanation: "Et sprogcenter" means "a language center". It is built from "et sprog" (a language) and "et center" (a center).

et spyd.explanation: "Et spyd" means "a spear". When you talk about the athletics event, the same word means "javelin": "at kaste spyd" (to throw the javelin).

et spædbarn.explanation: "Et spædbarn" means "an infant". The plural is "spædbørn" (infants), because "et barn" (a child) has the plural "børn" (children).

et spøgelse.explanation: "Et spøgelse" means "a ghost". It comes from the verb "at spøge" (to haunt). To say a place is haunted, say: "Det spøger i det gamle hus" (The old house is haunted).

et spørgeskema.explanation: "Et spørgeskema" means "a questionnaire". It is built from "at spørge" (to ask) and "et skema" (a chart or form).

et spørgsmål.explanation: "Et spørgsmål" means "a question". To ask permission to ask something, say: "Må jeg stille et spørgsmål?" (May I ask a question?) Literally, it says "May I put a question?"

et spørgsmålstegn.explanation: "Et spørgsmålstegn" means "a question mark". It is built from "et spørgsmål" (a question) and "et tegn" (a sign). When you mean a sign in general, "tegn" is used alone: "et tegn på forår" (a sign of spring).

et stadie.explanation: "Et stadie" means "a stage", as in one step in a process. To say where an actor stands in a theater, use "en scene" (a stage): "Skuespilleren står på scenen" (The actor stands on the stage).

et stadion.explanation: "Et stadion" means "a stadium". To say where a concert takes place, say: "Koncerten er på stadion" (The concert is at the stadium).

et standpunkt.explanation: "Et standpunkt" means "a point of view". To say you form your own opinion on something, use "at tage standpunkt til" (to take a position on): "Man må tage standpunkt til spørgsmålet" (You have to take a position on the question).

et statsborgerskab.explanation: "Et statsborgerskab" means "a citizenship". It is built from "en stat" (a state) and "en borger" (a citizen). To say you apply for it, use "at ansøge om" (to apply for): "Han ansøger om dansk statsborgerskab" (He is applying for Danish citizenship).

et stearinlys.explanation: "Et stearinlys" means "a candle". It is built from "stearin" (candle wax) and "lys" (light).

et sted.explanation: "Et sted" means "a place". To say you saw something somewhere, use "et sted": "Jeg har set det et sted" (I have seen it somewhere). To say somewhere else, add "andet" (other): "Vi kan spise et andet sted" (We can eat somewhere else).

et stedord.explanation: "Et stedord" means "a pronoun". It is built from "et sted" (a place) and "et ord" (a word), so it is literally a place word.

et stik.explanation: "Et stik" means "a plug", as in the electrical plug on a cord. When a needle or an insect pricks you, it means "a sting": "Et stik fra en bi gør ondt" (A sting from a bee hurts). To say you pull the plug out of the wall, use "at trække stikket ud" (to pull the plug out): "Træk stikket ud" (Pull the plug out).

et stillads.explanation: "Et stillads" means "scaffolding". To say workers are putting it up, use "at rejse" (to put up): "De rejser stillads om huset" (They are putting up scaffolding around the house).

et sting.explanation: "Et sting" means "a stitch", as in one loop of thread in sewing. To say you have a pain in your side from running, use "sidestik" (side stitch) instead: "Jeg har sidestik" (I have a stitch in my side).

et stipendium.explanation: "Et stipendium" means "a scholarship". To say you apply for one, use "at søge" (to apply for): "Hun søger et stipendium" (She is applying for a scholarship).

et stof.explanation: "Et stof" means "a fabric". When you talk about cloth for sewing, it means "a fabric": "Stoffet er blødt" (The fabric is soft). When you talk about a chemical or a drug, it means "a substance": "Det er et farligt stof" (It is a dangerous substance).

et stoppested.explanation: "Et stoppested" means "a stop", as in where a bus or train stops. It is built from "at stoppe" (to stop) and "et sted" (a place). To say a bus stop, put "bus" in front: "et busstoppested" (a bus stop).

et storindkøb.explanation: "Et storindkøb" means "a big grocery shop". It is built from "stor" (big) and "indkøb" (a purchase). To say you go grocery shopping, use "at købe ind" (to shop): "Vi skal købe ind i aften" (We are going grocery shopping tonight).

et stormagasin.explanation: "Et stormagasin" means "a department store". It is built from "stor" (big) and "et magasin" (a store). In Denmark, "Magasin" is also the name of a well-known department store in Copenhagen.

et straffespark.explanation: "Et straffespark" means "a penalty kick". It is built from "en straf" (a punishment) and "et spark" (a kick). To say a player scores from one, use "at score på" (to score from): "Han scorer på straffespark" (He scores from a penalty kick).

et strygebræt.explanation: "Et strygebræt" means "an ironing board". It is built from "at stryge" (to iron) and "et bræt" (a board). The same "bræt" is in "et skærebræt" (a cutting board).

et strygejern.explanation: "Et strygejern" means "an iron", as in the one for clothes. It is built from "at stryge" (to iron) and "jern" (the metal iron), so literally it is an ironing iron.

et strømstik.explanation: "Et strømstik" means "a power plug". It is built from "strøm" (electric power) and "et stik" (a plug). To say you unplug something, use "at trække stikket ud" (to pull the plug out): "Træk stikket ud" (Pull the plug out).

et studie.explanation: "Et studie" means "a study", as in a piece of research. To say a university study program, use "et studium" (a study program) instead: "Hendes studium tager fem år" (Her study program takes five years).

et studiejob.explanation: "Et studiejob" means "a student job". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "et job" (a job). To say you work next to your studies, use "ved siden af" (next to): "Jeg har et studiejob ved siden af studiet" (I have a student job next to my studies).

et studiekort.explanation: "Et studiekort" means "a student card". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "et kort" (a card). "Kort" also appears in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

et studielån.explanation: "Et studielån" means "a student loan". In Denmark, "SU" is the monthly support from the state for students, and you can take a "studielån" on top of it.

et studieår.explanation: "Et studieår" means "an academic year". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "et år" (a year). To say which year you are in, use "i sit" (in your): "Han er i sit andet studieår" (He is in his second academic year).

et studium.explanation: "Et studium" means "a study program". Its form "studiet" is the same as for "et studie" (a study), so "studiet" can mean either "the study program" or "the study". To say a piece of research, use "et studie": "Studiet bygger på 500 personer" (The study is based on 500 people).

et stykke.explanation: "Et stykke" means "a piece". To name what the piece is of, put it after: "et stykke papir" (a piece of paper). When you give a price for each item, put "stykket" (the piece) after the amount: "ti kroner stykket" (ten kroner each).

et stød.explanation: "Et stød" means "a shock / jolt". When you talk about bad news, it means "a shock": "Nyheden var et stød" (The news was a shock). When you talk about a sudden bump, it means "a jolt": "Bilen fik et stød bagfra" (The car got a jolt from behind). In Danish pronunciation, "stød" is also the name of a short catch in the voice in some words.

et støtteparti.explanation: "Et støtteparti" means "a supporting party". It is built from "at støtte" (to support) and "et parti" (a party). In Denmark, the parliament is called "Folketinget", and a government without a majority there can rely on a supporting party.

et sugerør.explanation: "Et sugerør" means "a drinking straw". It is built from "at suge" (to suck) and "et rør" (a tube).

et suk.explanation: "Et suk" means "a sigh". The matching verb is "at sukke" (to sigh). To say someone sighs, use the verb: "Han sukker højt" (He sighs loudly).

et sundhedskort.explanation: "Et sundhedskort" means "a health insurance card". It is built from "sundhed" (health) and "et kort" (a card). "Kort" also appears in "et kreditkort" (a credit card).

et supermarked.explanation: "Et supermarked" means "a supermarket". It is built from "super" (super) and "et marked" (a market). "Marked" is also the word for a market or fair, as in "et julemarked" (a Christmas market).

et svar.explanation: "Et svar" means "an answer". To thank someone for replying, say: "Tak for svaret" (Thanks for the reply).

et svigt.explanation: "Et svigt" means "a betrayal / letdown". In the word "hjertesvigt" (heart failure), "svigt" means something stops working as it should.

et svin.explanation: "Et svin" means "a pig". Calling a person "et svin" is rude: "Han er et svin" (He is a swine). To talk about the meat, add "kød" (meat): "svinekød" (pork).

et sving.explanation: "Et sving" means "a turn / curve". To tell someone which turn to take when driving, use "at tage" (to take): "Tag første sving til højre" (Take the first turn on the right).

et sværd.explanation: "Et sværd" means "a sword". The word "sværd" also appears in "en sværdfisk" (a swordfish).

et sygehus.explanation: "Et sygehus" means "a hospital". It is built from "syg" (sick) and "et hus" (a house). "Et hospital" is another word for it.

et symbol.explanation: "Et symbol" means "a symbol". To say something is used as a symbol, use "som symbol for" (as a symbol of): "Duen bruges som symbol for fred" (The dove is used as a symbol of peace).

et symptom.explanation: "Et symptom" means "a symptom". To say you feel no signs of illness, use "at have" (to have): "Jeg har ingen symptomer" (I have no symptoms). When you mean a sign of a problem in general, use it for the problem: "Støjen er et symptom på noget større" (The noise is a symptom of something bigger).

et syn.explanation: "Et syn" means "a sight / vision". When you talk about something you see, it means "a sight": "Det var et smukt syn" (It was a beautiful sight). When you talk about your ability to see, it means "vision": "Mit syn er blevet dårligere" (My vision has become worse).

et synonym.explanation: "Et synonym" means "a synonym". To ask for another word with the same meaning, say: "Kender du et synonym for glad?" (Do you know a synonym for happy?) The opposite is "et antonym" (an antonym): "Stor og lille er antonymer" (Big and small are antonyms).

et synspunkt.explanation: "Et synspunkt" means "a viewpoint". To say you understand how someone sees something, use "forstå" (to understand): "Jeg forstår dit synspunkt" (I understand your viewpoint). Do not mix it up with "et standpunkt" (a position), the opinion you have decided on: "Det er mit standpunkt" (That is my position).

et system.explanation: "Et system" means "a system". To say you have a system for doing something, use "til" (for): "Vi har et system til at sortere affald" (We have a system for sorting waste).

et sår.explanation: "Et sår" means "a wound". When you talk about a sore in the mouth, it means "a sore": "Jeg har et sår i munden" (I have a sore in my mouth).

et sæde.explanation: "Et sæde" means "a seat", as in a place to sit. To name a chair in a room, use "en stol" (a chair): "Der står en stol ved bordet" (There is a chair at the table).

et sølvbryllup.explanation: "Et sølvbryllup" means "a silver wedding anniversary". It is built from "sølv" (silver) and "et bryllup" (a wedding). To say the 50-year anniversary, use "et guldbryllup" (a golden wedding): "De holder guldbryllup i dag" (They are celebrating their golden wedding today).

et søm.explanation: "Et søm" means "a nail". To say a screw that you turn in, use "en skrue" (a screw): "Jeg skruer en skrue i planken" (I screw a screw into the board). The word "søm" also means a seam in clothes, and then it takes "en": "Sømmen på bukserne er gået op" (The seam of the trousers has come apart).

saft.explanation: "Saft" means "a cordial". To say you dilute it, use "at blande" (to mix): "Jeg blander saft med koldt vand" (I mix cordial with cold water). Do not mix it up with "en juice" (a juice): "Jeg drikker en juice til morgenmad" (I drink a juice with breakfast).

saftevand.explanation: "Saftevand" means "diluted cordial". It is built from "saft" (cordial) and "vand" (water). To offer a choice of drinks, say: "Vil du have saftevand eller mælk?" (Do you want diluted cordial or milk?)

salt.explanation: "Salt" means "salt". To ask for some, use "noget" (some) and no article: "Kan jeg få noget salt?" (Can I have some salt?) When you talk about taste, it means "salty": "Suppen er for salt" (The soup is too salty).

saltet.explanation: "Saltet" means "salted". To say food has had salt added, use it before the noun: "saltet smør" (salted butter). "Saltet" is also "the salt": "Giv mig saltet" (Pass me the salt). Do not mix it up with "salt" (salty), a taste: "Suppen er for salt" (The soup is too salty).

samfundsfag.explanation: "Et samfundsfag" means "a social studies subject". It is built from "et samfund" (a society) and "et fag" (a subject). To say you are good at it, use "god til" (good at): "Hun er god til samfundsfag" (She is good at social studies).

samme.explanation: "Samme" means "same". To say something happens on the same day, put it before the noun: "samme dag" (the same day). To say "the same man", put "den", "det" or "de" (all three mean "the") before it: "den samme mand" (the same man). To answer a greeting with "you too", say "Det samme!" (The same!): "God weekend!" - "Det samme!" (Have a good weekend! - You too!)

sammen.explanation: "Sammen" means "together". To say people do something together, put it after the verb: "Vi spiser sammen" (We eat together). The opposite is "alene" (alone): "Jeg spiser alene" (I eat alone). To greet a group, use "alle sammen" (everyone): "Hej alle sammen!" (Hello everyone!)

sammenhold.explanation: "Et sammenhold" means "togetherness". It comes from "at holde sammen" (to stick together). To say something creates togetherness, use "at skabe" (to create): "Fælles spisning skaber sammenhold" (Eating together creates togetherness).

sammenhængende.explanation: "Sammenhængende" means "coherent". It comes from "at hænge sammen" (to hang together). To say a text hangs together, use it before the noun: "en sammenhængende tekst" (a coherent text). The opposite is "usammenhængende" (disconnected): "Hans svar var usammenhængende" (His answer was disconnected).

sammenhængskraft.explanation: "En sammenhængskraft" means "social cohesion". It is built from "sammenhæng" (connection) and "kraft" (strength). "Kraft" also appears in "et kraftværk" (a power plant).

sammenlignelig.explanation: "Sammenlignelig" means "comparable". To say what something is compared to, add "med" (with): "Hans løn er sammenlignelig med min" (His pay is comparable to mine).

sammensat.explanation: "Sammensat" means "composite". To say a word is made of two words, use it before the noun: "et sammensat ord" (a compound word). When a problem has many parts, it means "complex": "Det er et sammensat problem" (It is a complex problem). To say something is hard, use "kompliceret" (complicated): "en kompliceret regel" (a complicated rule).

samt.explanation: "Samt" means "as well as". To join the last item of a list, put it before that item: "Kaffe, te samt kage" (Coffee, tea as well as cake). To say simply "and", use "og" (and): "Kaffe og kage" (Coffee and cake).

samtidig.explanation: "Samtidig" means "at the same time". To say two things happen together, put it after the verb: "De kom samtidig" (They arrived at the same time). To name the other event, add "med" (with): "samtidig med mødet" (at the same time as the meeting).

samtlige.explanation: "Samtlige" means "all", and stresses that none are left out: "samtlige elever" (every single student). To say simply "all", use "alle" (all): "Alle elever er her" (All the students are here).

sand.explanation: "Sand" means "sand". The adjective "sand" (true) is spelled the same. To say something is true, use "sandt" with "det" (it): "Det er sandt" (That is true).

sandaler.explanation: "Sandaler" means "sandals". To talk about only one, use "en sandal" (a sandal): "Jeg mistede en sandal" (I lost a sandal).

sandelig.explanation: "Sandelig" means "indeed". It comes from "sand" (true). To add emphasis to a statement, put it after the verb: "Det var sandelig dejligt" (That was indeed lovely).

sandsynlig.explanation: "Sandsynlig" means "likely". It is built from "sand" (true) and "synlig" (visible). To say something is likely to happen, use "sandsynligt" with "det" (it) and "at": "Det er sandsynligt, at det regner" (It is likely that it will rain).

sandsynligvis.explanation: "Sandsynligvis" means "probably". It is built from "sandsynlig" (likely). To answer a question with "probably not", say: "Kommer han?" - "Sandsynligvis ikke." (Is he coming? - Probably not.)

sankthans.explanation: "Sankthans" means "Midsummer". It is written together from "Sankt Hans" (Saint John). In Denmark, people light a bonfire on the evening of 23 June and sing "Midsommervisen" (the Midsummer song).

sarkastisk.explanation: "Sarkastisk" means "sarcastic". To say something nice about something bad, as a joke, speak in a flat voice: "Dejligt, det regner igen!" (Lovely, it is raining again!)

sej.explanation: "Sej" means "cool". When you talk about a strong person who does not give up, it means "tough": "Hun er sej" (She is tough). When you talk about food that is hard to chew, it means "tough": "sejt kød" (tough meat).

sejlads.explanation: "En sejlads" means "a sailing trip". It comes from "at sejle" (to sail), which is used for any trip by ship or boat: "Vi sejler med færgen til Bornholm" (We take the ferry to Bornholm).

seks.explanation: "Seks" means "six". English speakers may write it with "x", but it is spelled with "ks": "seks børn" (six children). To say someone's age, use it before "år" (years): "Hun er seks år" (She is six years old).

seksten.explanation: "Seksten" means "sixteen". To tell it apart from "seks" (six), note the difference between "seks børn" (six children) and "seksten børn" (sixteen children).

seksuel.explanation: "Seksuel" means "sexual". To say sexy, use "sexet" (sexy) instead: "en sexet kjole" (a sexy dress).

selleri.explanation: "Selleri" means "celery". To name the green stalks, use "stangselleri" (celery stalks). To name the round root, use "knoldselleri" (celeriac).

selv.explanation: "Selv" means "myself". To say you do something without help, put it after the verb: "Jeg gør det selv" (I do it myself). It stays the same for every person: "Hun gør det selv" (She does it herself). When it starts a sentence, it means "even": "Selv børn kan det" (Even children can do it).

selv tak.explanation: "Selv tak" means "you're welcome". Literally, it means "thanks yourself". To answer someone who thanks you for help, say: "Tak for hjælpen." - "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. - You're welcome.) When someone thanks you for last night, it also returns the thanks: "Tak for i aftes." - "Selv tak." (Thanks for last night. - Thanks to you too.)

selvforsvar.explanation: "Et selvforsvar" means "self-defense". It is built from "selv" (self) and "et forsvar" (a defense). In law, use "nødværge" (legal self-defense) instead: "Han handlede i nødværge" (He acted in self-defense).
